Classified as Academic Student Employees, our teaching assistants enjoy generous benefits, union representation, and a tuition waiver. Incoming MA students are also automatically considered for a one-time Top Scholar Research Assistant award, payable over one year. In their second year, they are eligible for a Taft Graduate Enhancement Fellowship, to support their project work.

[2, 3] Students are, therefore, required to complete a reasonable amount of work in every major field. [2, 3] Recipients of the doctoral degree are qualified to teach courses in Classics, western civilization and interdisciplinary courses. [2, 3] The course offerings are extensive. [2] Topics range from Bronze Age Greece to late Roman history, from Homer to later Latin literature. [2, 3] There is also the opportunity to work in other disciplines. [3] This is a funded, four-year, full-time program that results in a doctorate in Communication. [2, 3] Students receive academic training in various approaches to communication and have the opportunity to make connections with social justice issues and organizations through built-in research externship experiences. [2] The program is designed for students trained in communication theories, research, and practice who want to apply their expertise to a career in academia, industry, or social work that deals with issues of social justice. [2] The program's vision is to create a community of scholars dedicated to the study and practice of communication, with a deep concern for social justice issues in the local community and their global applications. [2] The PhD level of study emphasizes preparation for careers in college-level teaching, research and professional service. [2] PhD students are expected to complete course work in a major area of focus and to demonstrate, through a dissertation, contribution to knowledge in the areas of speech, language and hearing science, speech language pathology, or audiology. [2] Students must also complete coursework in pedagogical techniques, supervision and lab management, and grant-writing and are expected to engage in mentored teaching experiences. [2] Students have the opportunity to interact with doctoral-level faculty in Communication Sciences & Disorders, faculty in other departments and adjunct faculty in the community, who provide expertise and research mentoring in a wide variety of scientific and clinical aspects of communication sciences and disorders. [2] During the program, students will create an individualized plan of study in consultation with an advisor and academic committee. [2] This plan will constitute a road map for acquisition of expertise in the major area of focus as well as additional research and pedagogical skills. [2]
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati and all regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [8] Whether you aspire to a career in academia or agency-based research, the University of Cincinnati, as one of the top ranked programs in the nation, can help you reach your goals. [8] Our Doctor of Philosophy in Criminal Justice immerses students in a comprehensive curriculum designed to sharpen your analytical skills, hone your research acumen and foster a deep understanding of the complex issues within criminal justice. [8] The Criminal Justice faculty has devoted considerable time to designing a curriculum that will firmly ground doctoral students in the core of the discipline of criminal justice/criminology. [17, 18] The curriculum is structured around four main components: required coursework, an independent research paper, a comprehensive examination, and a dissertation. [17] The program, which admits new students every other year, features small class sizes to facilitate close interaction with faculty. [18] The Economics concentration includes two semesters of microeconomic theory, two semesters of econometrics, one semester of macroeconomic theory, and one semester of mathematical economics. [17]

Description: The Doctor of Philosophy in Geography is a 4-to-5-year graduate program that prepares students in geographic research and teaching. Our program is research-focused, and designed for students seeking a career in academia, and for public, private, and non-profit sector positions that require advanced research skills. [2] The PhD program is designed to prepare students for positions in college and university teaching and positions in the public and private sectors that require advanced research skills. [2] The program of study leads to: Broad knowledge of the discipline of geography; Broad knowledge of a subfield of geography and its literature; Specific expertise (deep knowledge) in the subfield. [2] PhD students must specialize in one of the research areas where the department has in-depth competence. These include GIScience, urban/economic, cultural, and physical and environmental geography. [10] Doctoral students complete required coursework within the department, including a mastery of at least one computer-based geographic technique (e.g. GIS, remote sensing, or computer cartography), quantitative methods, and a series of graduate seminars. [10] PhD students also complete coursework for a minor outside of geography. [10] Students demonstrate proficiency in a foreign language other than English or an approved computer science technique. [10] Students pass written comprehensive examinations demonstrating a broad mastery of the field and in their area of specialization, and pass an oral defense of their dissertation proposal. [10] Student then complete a dissertation embodying original research. [10]

The Molecular Pharmacology program is highly integrative and includes research specialization in the areas of molecular biology, biochemistry, cellular and subcellular biology, neurobiology, electrophysiology, cardiovascular biology, physiology, genetics, genomics and proteomics, bioinformatics, biomedical engineering, biophysics and structural biology. [1] Research projects typically employ approaches at the subcellular, cellular, organ and whole animal levels. The program is academically rigorous and students with a high level of achievement in biology, chemistry, pharmacology, biochemistry, physics, engineering or pharmacy are encouraged to apply. The Ph.D. program typically requires 4-5 years of study (no MS necessary). [1] Students primarily take didactic courses and rotate in research lab the first year (3 rotations required). Students participate in departmental and college seminars, journal clubs and begin their dissertation research work the second year, after qualification. [1]

ProgramName: PhD in Molecular Genetics, Biochemistry and Microbiology
Requirements: Candidates for the doctoral program are expected to have a strong undergraduate background in biology, chemistry, physics and mathematics with an overall GPA of at least 3.2 on a 4.0 scale. [2] GREs are not required, but highly recommended. We will waive the GRE requirement for applicants who demonstrate a strong record in relevant STEM courses such as organic chemistry, biochemistry, physical chemistry, molecular genetics, etc and have attained an overall STEM GPA of >3.5. [2] Your references will be asked via email to submit a recommendation letter for you using the online submission system. [2] You will not need to provide them with any forms, but you WILL need to provide all of their contact information in your online application. [2] Transcripts for all College Level Work. [2]
Department: College of Medicine
Fees.1: Full remission of tuition
Concentration: ['Cancer Biology & Regenerative Medicine', 'Cardiovascular Biology and Biochemistry', 'Microbiology and Immunology', 'Structural Biology']
Description: In modulates the Doctoral Program in Molecular Genetics, Biochemistry and Microbiology, academic requirements are divided into two areas: course work and dissertation research studies. [2] Students typically complete all necessary course work during Years 1 and 2 to allow them to focus their time on research during the remainder of their graduate studies. [2] Students should anticipate the completion of their graduate work in about five years of full-time study. [2] The minimum requirement for a doctoral degree from the University of Cincinnati is three years of full-time graduate study. [2] Eligibility for graduation requires a minimum of 90 graduate credits, the last 30 of which must be completed at the University of Cincinnati. [2] The program provides multiple laboratory opportunities in the molecular aspects of modern biomedical research, and is complemented by an extensive choice of courses across the disciplines of molecular genetics, biochemistry, microbiology, immunology, and bioinformatics. [1, 3] The research programs are developed in several focus areas namely: cancer biology and regenerative medicine, cardiovascular biology and biochemistry, microbiology and immunology, and structural biology. [1, 3] Many individual research programs directly impact questions of human biology and disease. [1, 3] Thus, the doctoral program offers diverse opportunities in research while integrating the fundamental knowledge base required for tomorrow's biomedical scientist, providing training and experience that is second-to-none. [1, 3]

ProgramName: PhD in Music
Requirements: Applicants to the PhD in Music at the University of Cincinnati's College-Conservatory of Music (CCM) must complete the university's graduate application and then submit pre-screening materials through the CCM's Acceptd portal. A 500-word personal statement is a required component of the university application. This statement should cover your degree objectives, a frank assessment of your professional and personal strengths and weaknesses, and any significant professional experiences or honors. The number of letters of recommendation varies by specific program, with some requiring two to three letters. Unofficial transcripts from all previously attended institutions are also required. Specific requirements for each specialization (Composition, Musicology, and Music Theory) are detailed on the Acceptd portal.
Department: College-Conservatory of Music
Fees.1: {'in-state': '$8,129/Term', 'out-of-state': None}
Description: The Ph.D. in music with an emphasis in musicology is designed to provide a comprehensive course of study in the history, literature and philosophy of music and related subject areas beyond the level required for the master’s degree. [22] The program trains students to contribute to scholarly and artistic fields as researchers, pedagogues, writers, future educational administrators, and musicians, emphasizing ethnographic, historical, and analytical methods for studying any musical tradition. [24] Students have opportunities to relate ethnomusicological research with performance or approaches from music theory, music education, music therapy, composition, and music production. [24] For Ph.D. students, the development of a "cognate" (a secondary area of specialization) is encouraged in disciplines outside of the conservatory. [24]
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati and all regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [6]
CostPerCredit: $813/Credit Hour
ScholarshipAmount: up to full tuition

ProgramName: PhD in Music Education
Department: College-Conservatory of Music
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy in Music Education is designed to prepare scholars, researchers, and leaders for positions in music teacher education, music education research, P-12 music teaching and leadership, and music education policy. [1] The coursework is interdisciplinary in nature, drawing on the expertise of the faculty at SMTD as well as cross-campus faculty in a wide array of specialties. Designed for students seeking the highest degree in the field, the PhD is a rigorous course of study culminating in a doctoral dissertation. [1] Two years of coursework are required. The core curriculum includes: music education, music theory, musicology. [1] Additional coursework can include theory, musicology, composition, performing arts technology or jazz studies. [1]

ProgramName: PhD in Neuroscience
Requirements: Prospective students are expected to have a Bachelor's degree or above and have completed a curriculum that includes course work in some or all of these areas: biology, physics, mathematics, chemistry, psychology, neuroscience, and other appropriate scientific disciplines. Applicants are expected to have a minimum 3.0 GPA. The Committee evaluates research experience, past publications, letters of recommendation, personal and educational statements, and grades. [2]
Department: College of Medicine
Fees.1: Full tuition scholarships are provided to all admitted students in the PhD in Neuroscience program. [31]
Concentration: ['Stress & Neuropsychiatric Disorders', 'Developmental Neurobiology', 'Pain', 'Sensory Neuroscience', 'Stroke & Neural Trauma', 'Metabolism & Obesity', 'Epilepsy', 'Cognitive Development', 'Motivation & Drugs of Abuse']
Description: The Neuroscience Graduate Program at the University of Cincinnati was established in 1988 as an interdisciplinary program offering the PhD degree and now has more than 80 participating faculty members from 22 departments in the Colleges of Medicine, Pharmacy, and Arts & Sciences. [2] The program supports study in a wide range of Neuroscience-related research areas, including but not limited to neural development; neurobiology of addiction; biology of neurological diseases and neurodegeneration; neuroimaging; neuroendocrinology of stress, obesity and diabetes; and cognitive neuroscience. [10] Ph.D. Neuroscience students take lecture and laboratory courses; learn to read, understand, and present current scientific literature; develop and carry out substantial original research, and present their research at meetings and conferences, including the annual Neuroscience retreat each Spring. [3] During the first year, all students participate in a unique year-long Core Course that surveys current neuroscience. The subjects covered in lectures are accompanied by direct experience in the lab. [3] In addition to scholarship and laboratory training in high impact research within state-of-the-art facilities, the Neuroscience Graduate Program offers guidance and support for a wide range of professional careers. [2] Competitive stipends, tuition scholarships, and health insurance are provided to all admitted students. [2]
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati and all regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [10]
ScholarshipType: Tuition scholarships, competitive stipends, and health insurance are provided to all admitted students. [31] Distinguished graduate fellowships are also available. [31]

ProgramName: PhD in Nursing
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree in nursing or a master's degree in nursing, or a master's degree in a health care-related field, and demonstrate the potential to develop new scientific knowledge related to nursing and/or health care.
Department: College of Nursing
Description: The PhD in Nursing at the University of Cincinnati is a research-based doctoral program designed to prepare nurses for careers in research and higher education. The program's courses are structured to provide the foundation for a nursing research career, where students partner with faculty mentors in their area of research interest to develop a program of research that contributes to the creation of nursing knowledge. The curriculum focuses on scholarship and nursing research, with coursework heavily geared toward advanced scientific research principles, data analysis, and statistics. For full-time students, the initial two years are dedicated to coursework, while the third year is focused on independent research. The program can be completed on a full- or part-time basis.
Accredidation: The baccalaureate, Master of Science in Nursing, Doctor of Nursing Practice, and post-graduate APRN certificate programs at the University of Cincinnati College of Nursing are accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE).

ProgramName: PhD in Pathobiology and Molecular Medicine
Requirements: Complete the UC Graduate Admissions Application, including: Personal Statement Essay; Transcript from an accredited college or university with at least a B average; Three letters of recommendation from people familiar with your academic record; International Applicants only: Proof of English language proficiency. [1]
Department: College of Medicine
Fees: Full tuition remission
Description: The graduate program in Pathobiology & Molecular Medicine offers a course of study in biomedical research leading to a Ph.D. degree. The program is administered by two clinical departments: Pathology and Internal Medicine. Pathology is a branch of medical science concerning the study of the nature of human disease and its causes, whereas machine is concerned with therapeutic strategies to prevent or cure human diseases. Doctoral students in the Pathobiology & Molecular Medicine graduate program are exposed to each of these disciplines in a program of study that unites contemporary investigative research in biomedical sciences with an understanding of human disease and the challenges that face effective treatment.
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati and all regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [2]
ScholarshipAmount: $30,000/year stipend

ProgramName: PhD in Pharmacology and Systems Physiology
Requirements: Prospective students must have a baccalaureate degree from an accredited undergraduate institution and a strong background in the sciences. Students are expected to have an overall GPA of at least 3.0, with particular emphasis placed on having excellent performance in the advanced science courses. [1]
Department: College of Medicine, Department of Pharmacology and Systems Physiology
Fees.1: Full tuition scholarship
Description: Our doctoral (PhD) degree program is designed to provide training for the next generation of scientists, innovators and leaders in pharmacology and physiology. [3] Students will engage in a contemporary curriculum including thesis research training in faculty-mentored research programs. [3] Alumni of our training program have advanced to successful careers in academia, industry, and governmental organizations. [3] Faculty research programs offer students a wide array of choices for thesis research projects. [3] These research programs involve mechanistic and quantitative aspects of potential and established drug targets, analysis of normal and pathological physiological processes, and development of new biotechnologies for high-impact disease interventions through the use of state-of-the-art biotechnology and pharmacological methods. [3] Student thesis projects may include mechanistic and computational analyses of: cardiovascular biology; neurobiology; chronobiology; metabolic biology; immunology; membrane transport; molecular pharmacology of proteins/enzymes; molecular biology of hormones, enzymes, ion channels, & regulatory proteins; cancer biology; environmental toxicology; translational approaches; protein chemistry & structural biology; gene therapy; stem cell therapy; etc. [3] A variety of approaches from single molecules to entire organisms are used to study mechanisms in health and disease. [3]

ProgramName: PhD in Pharmacy
Requirements: Applicants with an undergraduate degree in chemistry, biology, engineering, or related fields from a regionally accredited institution are eligible to apply for our full-time, research-intensive PhD program in Pharmaceutical Sciences. [11] Similarly, those with a completed professional degree like PharmD, MD, or DVM also meet eligibility requirements. [11] Interested applicants can directly apply without prior completion of an MS degree. [11] Admission to our competitive program, which offers supervised, full-time research training, is based on a selective process. [11] Three letters of recommendation are required, and we strongly recommend that applicants seek letters from individuals who can provide insights into their research experience. [11]
Department: College of Pharmacy
Concentration: ['Biomembrane Sciences Track', 'Experimental Therapeutics Track', 'Health Outcomes Track']
Description: The PhD in Pharmaceutical Sciences program is designed to inspire and challenge, with a comprehensive curriculum that combines cutting-edge coursework with advanced research. Students can delve into captivating areas such as pioneering drug development, unraveling the intricate impact of medications on the body, exploring breakthrough drug delivery techniques, and maximizing the therapeutic potential of medications for optimal patient outcomes. Flexible scheduling options are available, including online and in-person formats, allowing students to tailor their learning experience. The program aims to train interdisciplinary scholars in pharmaceutical sciences, economics, business, and quantitative analysis. By conducting research in this emerging field, students develop expertise that can improve patient health.
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati and all regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [2, 11]

ProgramName: PhD in Philosophy
Requirements: Required application materials as part of the online application include the following: A writing sample. A statement of purpose. Three letters of recommendation. Undergraduate (and if applicable, graduate) transcript(s). [6]
Description: The Philosophy Department curriculum covers most areas in contemporary philosophical problems as well as most of the major periods in the history of philosophy. [2] The department is especially strong in philosophy of mind and philosophy of the life sciences. [2] The Ph.D. program in Philosophy offers two tracks, the Traditional Track and the Sciences Track. [2] Students in the Sciences Track do graduate work in a science and write an interdisciplinary dissertation. [2] The graduate program is a relatively small one which allows close working relationships between faculty and graduate students. [2] In recent years, the ratio of faculty to funded graduate students has been nearly one to one. [2] Distinguished visiting speakers are brought to the department on a regular basis. [2] The department hosts an annual colloquium, which brings in up to a dozen scholars focused on a specific theme. [2]
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati and all regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [2, 14]

ProgramName: PhD in Physics
Department: College of Arts and Sciences
Description: The University of Cincinnati has a long and distinguished tradition of research and graduate education – it was the first institution west of the Appalachian Mountains to offer a PhD degree in physics. [2] The physics graduate program emphasizes cutting edge research and education, resulting in orginal published work, and preparing our students for university, national lab, or industrial/corporate employment. [3, 6] The graduate program focuses mainly on the PhD. [7] Graduate students play a key role in the research and teaching missions of the Physics Department, and work closely with faculty advisors. [2] Physics faculty work closely with graduate students, mentoring them in a variety of areas, including condensed matter, high energy, and particle physics, astrophysics, physics education, etc. [3, 6] In addition to the research areas inside the department, interdisciplinary options in chemistry, medical imaging, physics education, and engineering are available. [7]
ScholarshipType: awards which cover both tuition and living expenses

ProgramName: PhD in Political Science
Requirements: Transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate work; Three letters of recommendation; A statement of purpose explaining why you have decided to pursue graduate education in political science and specifically addressing how your interests fit with those of the department faculty. [2]
Department: School of Public and International Affairs
Fees.1: $14,902 per year for Ohio residents, $26,674 per year for out-of-state students.
Description: The PhD in Political Science prepares students for careers in education and research at the university level. We make every effort to ensure our doctoral students receive the breadth and depth of training that will enable them to excel as leaders in the discipline. We strive to create a demographically and ideologically diverse student body within our graduate program. [1] Students pursuing the Ph.D. in political science at UC's School of Public and International Affairs select two of the following major fields of study: American Politics, Comparative Politics, International Relations, or Research Methodology. [2] The Political Science Ph.D. program prepares students for careers in research, teaching, public policy, government, or international organizations. [2] Recent graduates work in the US and internationally in colleges and universities, governments, and research firms. [2]
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati and all regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [2]
CostPerCredit: $662 for Ohio residents, $1,249 for out-of-state students.

ProgramName: PhD in Psychology
Requirements: To submit an application for the Psychology program, please visit our Admissions Requirements page and complete the UC Graduate Admissions Application. [2] The application deadline for Fall enrollment is December 5th. [2] Required materials include: a Bachelors degree (psychology major preferred), a minimum of 16 semester credit hours (or 24 quarter credit hours) in non-introductory undergraduate psychology courses, at least one course in research methods in the behavioral or social sciences, at least one course in statistical methods, 3 letters of recommendation, a Personal Statement, a current CV or resume, and unofficial transcripts. [2, 3] Previous research experience is strongly recommended. [2]
Department: College of Arts and Sciences
Description: The University of Cincinnati Department of Psychology trains doctoral-level researchers, primarily in the areas of health psychology, behavioral and human factors, and neuropsychology. [2] Additionally, prospective students with interests outside these areas may apply for admission if their interests correspond closely to those of at least one faculty member. [2] Students are admitted to the program to work with a specific faculty mentor. [2] Mentors are responsible for ensuring students are actively engaged in research from the beginning of graduate school and that this work leads successfully to a dissertation. [2] Our goal is to train students to compete effectively for positions in a broad variety of settings. [2] We provide extensive professional development opportunities during doctoral training. [2]  Students in the clinical program are expected to develop expertise in both research and clinical practice. Graduates of the program hold faculty positions in colleges and universities, research positions in hospitals and research institutes, and clinical positions in community mental health centers, industry, and penal systems or have independent practices. [15]
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati and all regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [2] The Clinical Psychology track of our program has been continuously accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of the American Psychological Association, 750 First St. NE, Washington, DC 20002-4242, since 1948. [15]

ProgramName: PhD in Public Health
Requirements: In addition to a completed application and fee, the following are required: CV or resume, a Statement of Purpose, and unofficial transcripts for all higher education institutions attended. Three letters of recommendation are also required. For PhD applicants specifically, information about prior research experience (on average, in hours per week for the past year) is needed. [10]
Department: College of Medicine
Concentration: ['Epidemiology', 'Environmental & Industrial Hygiene', 'Environmental Genetics & Molecular Toxicology', 'Occupational Safety & Ergonomics']
Description: The Department of Environmental & Public Health Sciences offers several doctoral programs. The Epidemiology program focuses on the study of the distribution and determinants of disease and injury in human populations, with an emphasis on environmental, occupational, clinical, quantitative, community, molecular and genetic epidemiology. [2] The Environmental & Industrial Hygiene and Occupational Safety & Ergonomics programs teach students to anticipate, recognize, evaluate, and design programs to control harmful exposures in environmental or occupational settings. [2] The Environmental Genetics & Molecular Toxicology program's curriculum highlights the genetic and molecular mechanisms that underlie diseases related to the environment. [2]
Accredidation: The Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH) accredits the public health programs at the University of Cincinnati. [9] The University of Cincinnati is also accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [5]

ProgramName: PhD in Romance Languages and Literatures
Department: College of Arts and Sciences
Concentration: Spanish literature & cultural studies and Latin American literature & cultural studies
Description: Ph. D. students are encouraged to develop their own particular doctoral curriculum according to their fields of interest and to the topic of their dissertation. At the Ph. D. level, we teach and model the complex critical and theoretical skills necessary to conduct literary research. [2] With our nationally recognized language-instructor training and our careful mentoring in research methods, we prepare doctoral students for success in college-level teaching positions; our placement rate is excellent. [2]
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati and all regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [2]
ScholarshipType: Graduate Assistantships, which include a stipend and a full or partial tuition scholarship.

ProgramName: PhD in Sociology
Requirements: Admission requirements for the PhD in Sociology at the University of Cincinnati include unofficial or official transcripts from all undergraduate and any M.A. or M.S. degree programs, a resume or curriculum vitae, and a statement of purpose. Applicants must also submit a sample of their best academic writing and three letters of recommendation. The university requires a minimum GPA of 3.0, but this can be waived if the Department and Graduate School agree.
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy in Sociology provides training in theory and research methods beyond the MA. The department at UC is a vibrant intellectual space, centered in the multiple research projects of our faculty members and students. We specialize in the study of social inequality, specifically in the areas of community and urban sociology, health and medicine, race and ethnicity, and gender and sexuality. We encourage prospective graduate students interested in these issues to join us! [5] The PhD program provides both teaching and research experience for students in the course of their graduate work. Most graduates get academic jobs, but some choose research-oriented jobs in government or the private sector. [5]
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati and all regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [5, 11]

ProgramName: PhD in Spanish
Requirements:
A recent MA degree or its equivalent from an accredited college or university, preferably an MA in Spanish or French and a strong literary background.
A good foundation in Spanish or French language and literature.
A minimum GPA of 3.50.
GRE not required.
Curriculum Vitae (CV, resume, hoja de vida)
Three letters of recommendation, preferably from recent language or literature professors submitted through the UC online recommendation system.
Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended.
A 500 word statement of purpose, preferably in the target language.
A writing sample in the target language.
Department: College of Arts and Sciences, Department of Romance and Arabic Languages and Literatures
Concentration: ['Spanish Literature and Cultural Studies', 'Latin American Literature and Cultural Studies']
Description: The PhD program in Romance Languages and Literatures with a specialization in Spanish aims to train versatile scholars and experienced teachers. It is a pioneer in accepting creative dissertations alongside research-based ones and prepares doctoral students for success in college-level teaching or other professional opportunities. The program is committed to fostering interdisciplinary and cross-cultural exchanges and conversations on current European, Francophone, and Latin American issues.

ProgramName: PhD in Special Education
Description: In the Special Education concentration within the Educational Studies Ph.D. program, doctoral students learn via a host of hands-on experiential opportunities, including: Working with students of all ages with mild disabilities in urban, suburban and rural school districts in the K-12 setting and across all academic subjects; Participating in inter-disciplinary research with other fields such as school, cognitive, clinical and community psychology, as well as speech and language pathology; Partnering with organizations like Cincinnati Children's Hospital, Su Casa and the Greater Islamic Center of Cincinnati; Collaborating with researchers focused on behavior interventions in K-12 and post-secondary settings; Assisting students with mild disabilities as they transition to post-secondary settings.

ProgramName: Doctor of Audiology (AuD)
Description: TThe Doctor of Audiology (AuD) program at the University of Cincinnati is a three-year (nine-semester), full-time doctoral program designed to prepare students for careers as audiologists. [3, 9] The curriculum involves an in-depth study of hearing and balance disorders, combined with practical clinical experience starting from the first semester. [3] Coursework covers the full professional scope of practice, including topics like anatomy and physiology, assessment of hearing and balance, hearing aids, implantable hearing devices, and habilitative audiology. [3] The program culminates in a one-year, full-time clinical externship. [3] Students also have opportunities for unique experiences, such as international service trips and the option to pursue a certificate in animal audiology through the FETCHLAB. [3] Upon completion, graduates are prepared to work with patients of all ages in various settings, including private practices, hospitals, schools, and governmental agencies. [3]
Accredidation: The Doctor of Audiology (Au.D.) education program in audiology at the University of Cincinnati is accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology (CAA) of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association. [5] Additionally, the University of Cincinnati and all its regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (HLC). [3, 12]

ProgramName: Doctor of Education (EdD) in Urban Educational Leadership
Department: College of Education, Criminal Justice, and Human Services
Description: The Doctor of Education in Urban Educational Leadership program at the University of Cincinnati is dedicated to nurturing visionary educational leaders who possess the critical thinking and reflective skills needed to address complex issues in educational leadership and policy. [2] Our curriculum delves into these challenges at various levels of education, from local to state to federal, ensuring our students are well-equipped to make a difference. [2] In today's ever-evolving educational landscape, leaders, policymakers and administrators face an increasing array of challenges, many of which are closely tied to issues of equity and social justice. [2] The Urban Educational Leadership Ed. D. is a new online advanced degree at the University of Cincinnati designed for experienced educators and seasoned leaders who are passionate about revolutionizing education leadership. [2] Through the Urban Educational Leadership Ed.D. program, students will not only expand their expertise but can also opt for one of two specialized concentrations: K-12 Education or Higher Education. [2] Graduates will emerge with a profound understanding of best practices that promote equity and diversity in all aspects of education, positioning them as influential leaders in this ever-changing landscape. [2]
Accredidation: CAEP Accreditation [2]
ScholarshipType: Many students who are accepted into this program receive partial or complete funding towards this program.

ProgramName: Doctor of Medicine (MD)
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the University of Cincinnati College of Medicine, applicants must be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident. A minimum of 90 semester hours from an accredited U.S. four-year institution is required. Applicants should have a strong foundation in the sciences, with coursework typically including one-year courses in biology, general and organic chemistry, physics, and mathematics. Coursework in the social, cultural, and behavioral sciences is also highly recommended. [2] All applications must be submitted through the American Medical College Application Service (AMCAS). [5] A complete application includes the AMCAS application, a UC On-Line Secondary Application, letters of recommendation, and MCAT scores. [5]
Description: The University of Cincinnati College of Medicine's website does not provide a centralized, comprehensive description of the Doctor of Medicine (MD) program's objectives and curriculum. While the site mentions that the College of Medicine is dedicated to excellence in education, research, and patient care, a specific, detailed overview of the MD program was not found.
Accredidation: The Doctor of Medicine (MD) program at the University of Cincinnati College of Medicine is accredited by the Liaison Committee on Medical Education (LCME). [4, 6] The program was granted an eight-year term of accreditation. [4, 6]

ProgramName: Doctor of Musical Arts (DMA) in Composition
Requirements: CCM's Doctoral of Musical Arts in Composition (DMA) degree program is designed to provide a comprehensive course of study in the composition of music at the advanced level in both acoustic and electro acoustic mediums. [2] CCM's admission requirements vary by program. All programs require both the appropriate University application followed by a pre-screening submission via CCM's Acceptd website, which must be completed and uploaded by Dec. 1. [2] The DMA in composition helps students acquire competence in the broad range of endeavors characteristic of composing through the following requirements: Private lessons; Required courses in electronic music, music history, graduate research, and music electives in composition and other areas; DMA Recital; DMA Orals Presentation; DMA Analytical Presentation; DMA Dissertation. [2] For graduate programs, the university welcomes applications from students who hold a baccalaureate degree (or higher) from a college or university regarded as standard by a regional or general accrediting agency, and have at least a B average in undergraduate course work (or otherwise give evidence of promise that is judged satisfactory by the admitting program and the Graduate School). [5]
Department: College-Conservatory of Music
Fees: $750/Term
Fees.1: $750/Term
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music is an accredited institution of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). The Doctor of Musical Arts in Composition is listed as an accredited program.
CostPerCredit: $75/Credit Hour
ScholarshipType: Talent and merit-based Graduate Incentive Scholarships, Graduate Assistantships

ProgramName: Doctor of Musical Arts (DMA) in Conducting
Department: College-Conservatory of Music. [24, 27]
Fees.1: For the 2024-25 academic year, graduate tuition and fees were: In-State: $20,185 per year; Out of State: $31,927 per year; International: $32,177 per year.
Description: CCM's Department of Wind Studies offers both the Master of Music and Doctor of Musical Arts in Wind Conducting. The department also offers five ensembles for credit, including the CCM Wind Symphony, CCM Wind Ensemble, CCM Chamber Winds, CCM Musica Nova and CCM Brass Choir. Each ensemble meets two to three times per week and each performs six full programs annually. Each graduate conducting student conducts all five of these ensembles each year, supervised by Director of Wind Studies Kevin Michael Holzman. CCM is a college within the University of Cincinnati, a major undergraduate university and graduate research institution of more than 40,000 students. The synergy created by housing CCM within a comprehensive public university gives the college its unique character and defines its objective: to educate and inspire the whole artist and scholar for positions on the world's stage.
ScholarshipAmount: Graduate Incentive Scholarship amounts may range up to full tuition. [7]
ScholarshipType: Talent and merit-based Graduate Incentive Scholarships and University Graduate Assistantships are available. [7, 16]

CostPerCredit: In-state: $662, Out-of-state: $1,408. [3]

ProgramName: Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP)
Requirements: A current, active, unrestricted Registered Nurse (RN) licensure with no disciplinary action. Bachelor of Science in Nursing from an ACEN- (formerly NLNAC) or CCNE-accredited nursing institution. For Post-MSN DNP applicants only: a Master of Science in Nursing from an ACEN- or CCNE-accredited nursing institution. A minimum overall BSN GPA of 3.25 on a 4.0 scale is recommended. A minimum science GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (not required for Systems Leadership and Nursing Education MSN program applicants). A minimum undergraduate Statistics GPA of 2.0 on a 4.0 scale. [2, 3]
Concentration: ['Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner', 'Adult-Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioner', 'Family Nurse Practitioner', 'Nurse Anesthesia', 'Occupational Health Nursing', 'Pediatric Acute Care Nurse Practitioner', 'Psychiatric-Mental Health Nurse Practitioner', 'Public Health Nursing', 'Systems Leadership', 'Post-MSN Doctor of Nursing Practice']
Description: The Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) programs at UC College of Nursing prepare nurses to lead at the highest level of practice, improving patient outcomes and delivering high-quality, cost-effective care. Graduates learn to translate research into practice, drive quality improvement and lead health care systems, preparing for roles as nurse practitioners, clinical leaders, administrators and faculty. [10]
Accredidation: The Doctor of Nursing Practice program at the University of Cincinnati College of Nursing is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE). [8] The Doctor of Nursing Practice in Nurse Anesthesia is also accredited by the Council on Accreditation of Nurse Anesthesia Educational Programs (COA). [8]

ProgramName: Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD)
Requirements: To be considered a qualified candidate, applicants should have a strong academic background, a demonstrated history of leadership and involvement in community service, and strong essays and personal statements. [3] A preferred GPA is a minimum of 3.0. [3] The application process involves two stages: completing the PharmCAS application and a supplemental UC application. [4] Applicants must also complete the undergraduate pre-pharmacy curriculum with a “C” or better in all required courses. [3] Three letters of recommendation are required. [3]
Department: James L. Winkle College of Pharmacy
Fees: $27,964/Year (in-state) for P1-P3 students and $34,980/Year (in-state) for P4 students. $29,464/Year (out-of-state) for P1-P3 students and $36,480/Year (out-of-state) for P4 students. [9]

[5] Applicants must have graduated from an accredited high school, typically within the top one-third of their class, and submit an official high school transcript. [5] All applicants are required to submit pre-screening materials through the CCM's Acceptd website to be considered for an audition. [7] This pre-screening includes a headshot and resume, two contrasting song pieces, a monologue from a published play, and a dance video. [7] An optional "Wild Card" media submission is also allowed. [7]
Department: College-Conservatory of Music (CCM)
Fees: For the 2025-2026 academic year, annual tuition for Ohio residents is $14,394 and for non-residents is $29,728. [27] There is an additional College-Conservatory of Music program fee of $750 per term. [30]
Description: A four-year interdisciplinary bachelor of fine arts (BFA) program, it was used by the National Association of Schools of Theatre in formulating the guidelines for the accreditation of Musical Theatre programs nationwide. [7] The program provides professional conservatory training designed to help singers, dancers and actors become accomplished musical theatre performers. [7] Students are trained in voice, music, acting and dance. [7] They participate in productions and create a freshman and a senior showcase, the latter functioning as their New York debut for agents and casting. [7] At CCM, we are in the business of turning out "triple threats" -- talented young people who can sing, dance and act with equal accomplishment. [8] Our students contribute positively to the growth of the American musical theatre. [8] We encourage them to explore techniques beyond the spoken word to project dramatic ideas. [8] We make the non-literal an essential part of the creative and interpretive process. [8]
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music is an accredited institution of the National Association of Schools of Dance (NASD), the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM), the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST), and a member of the University/ Resident Theatre Association (U/RTA). [2] The University of Cincinnati and all regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [2]
CostPerCredit: For the 2025-2026 cohort, the cost per credit hour is $600 for Ohio residents and $1,239 for non-residents. [27]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based scholarships are available for students who apply by the Early Action deadline. [23]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Theatre Design and Production
Requirements: For first-year undergraduate admission, the University of Cincinnati requires the Common Application, a non-refundable application fee (or waiver), and an official or unofficial high school transcript. Letters of recommendation and ACT/SAT scores are listed as optional. [11] For graduate admissions, general requirements include an online application with a fee, and unofficial transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. [2] Many graduate programs may also ask for a CV/Resume, personal statement, and letters of recommendation, but these are not universal, institute-level requirements. [2, 9]
Department: College-Conservatory of Music (CCM)
Fees: $16,748/Year (Ohio Resident)
Concentration: ['Costume Design and Technology', 'Lighting Design and Technology', 'Sound Design and Technology', 'Stage Design, Props and Scenic Art', 'Stage Management', 'Technical Production']
Description: The University of Cincinnati's College-Conservatory of Music (CCM) offers a Bachelor of Fine Arts in Theatre Design and Production, described as "a training ground where aspiring theatre designers and technicians gain top-quality experience". [2] The program emphasizes hands-on, practical production work, allowing students significant flexibility beyond the core courses to focus on personal development. [3] The curriculum is dedicated to fostering the performing arts by mentoring and educating young theatre artists, integrating practical training in scenics, costumes, lighting, sound, stage management, wigs, and makeup. [3] The program's objective is to educate and inspire the whole artist and scholar for positions on the world's stage. [7, 9] Students are prepared for careers as performers, designers, directors, producers, and technicians in various facets of the entertainment industry. [8] The program is housed within state-of-the-art facilities, including extensive shops and studios, and offers students opportunities to work on a robust production season of musicals, plays, operas, and dance. [2, 8]
Accredidation: CCM's theatre programs are accredited by the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST). [8] The University of Cincinnati and all its regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [6, 8]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music in Commercial Music Production
Department: College-Conservatory of Music (CCM)
Fees: Estimated for 2026: $13,836/Year (In-State), $29,161/Year (Out-of-State). [7]
Description: CCM's bachelor of music degree in Commercial Music Production (CMP) offers a comprehensive education in professional commercial music studies. This unique program combines core training in music theory, composition, arranging and musicianship combined with recording studio techniques, commercial music and media technologies. Although this degree includes music production, editing, business and studio technical training, it is important to note that this is music degree, not a music technology, music industry, audio or recording degree. Successful CMP applicants are expected to have significant musical training and study. The CMP degree includes an additional emphasis on entrepreneurial business acumen by inclusion of a Minor in Entrepreneurship from UC's Lindner College of Business. This creates a vibrant and exclusive educational experience that provides graduates with numerous opportunities for meaningful employment in the music industry.
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music is an accredited institution of the National Association of Schools of Dance (NASD), the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM), the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST), and a member of the University/ Resident Theatre Association (U/RTA). The University of Cincinnati and all regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission.
AverageScholarshipAmount: On average, students receive $2,000 per year from the Cincinnatus Scholarship. [5]
CostPerCredit: $582 for Ohio residents (2024-25). [17]
ScholarshipAmount: The National Outreach Award provides $10,000 per year, and some Cincinnatus awards can cover full tuition and fees. [5]
ScholarshipType: Talent-based, Academic, and location-based scholarships are available. [5, 33]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music in Music Education
Description: CCM's Division of Music Education offers formal programs of study leading to the Bachelor of Music (BM) in Music Education, Master of Music (MM) in Music Education and Master of Music Education (MME). Drawing upon widely varied institutional and community resources, these programs integrate the high quality of music training and experience available in a conservatory environment with a strong program of pedagogical preparation. [6] Each year, CCM's Music Education program serves 80-90 students in residence in its undergraduate and graduate programs. [6] The objectives of the programs are to: integrate the high quality of music training and experience available in a conservatory environment with a strong program of liberal education and professional-pedagogical preparation, draw upon the diversity of music teaching settings within the Cincinnati community (i.e., urban and suburban, school-based and community-based), and be tailored to individual needs and interests through double degree options. [6] Graduates of these programs enjoy a 100% placement rate, most often as school music teachers, community arts personnel, church musicians, faculty members at colleges and universities, and students in advanced programs of study. [6]
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Music in Music Education program is listed as 'Accredited' by the University of Cincinnati. [4] The University of Cincinnati is an accredited institution of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM), and the Bachelor of Music in Music Education is listed as an accredited degree program. [3] The University of Cincinnati and all regional campuses are also accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (HLC). [2, 4]

[11] The application process for all students generally requires the submission of an online application, an application fee, and transcripts from all previously attended institutions. [3, 11, 13] Additional requirements such as letters of recommendation, a personal statement, or a resume/CV may be required for specific programs. [3, 7]

Description: Declared "one of this country's leading conservatories" by the New York Times, CCM provides life-changing experiences within a highly creative and multidisciplinary artistic environment. CCM's educational roots date back to 1867, and a solid, visionary instruction has been at its core since that time. The synergy created by housing CCM within a comprehensive public university gives the college its unique character and defines its objective: to educate and inspire the whole artist and scholar for positions on the world's stage. [2]
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music is an accredited institution of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). [2, 5, 7, 11]
ScholarshipType: Merit-Based, Need-Based, Demographic, Field of Study, Community Service

Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Music presents a special opportunity to pursue liberal arts study across the University of Cincinnati's many outstanding programs, while also drawing upon the benefits of studying music in a world-class conservatory environment. [2] The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Music program at CCM culminates in a liberal arts degree that provides students with flexible pathways for the study of music as a cultural and artistic practice. [2] After completing a core that focuses on listening, writing, and thinking about a wide array of music, students select classes in areas such as sound technologies, music and cultural history, ethnographic approaches, composition, analytical skills, and applied music-making. These experiences culminate in an individual capstone research project with a CCM faculty member. [2] CCM's BA in Music is a gateway to careers in music and allied fields, including music promotions, arts administration, music therapy, journalism, ethnomusicology, musicology, music theory, composition, songwriting, commercial music production, and library science. [2]
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music is an accredited institution of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). [3, 6] The University of Cincinnati and all regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Advanced Medical Imaging Technology
Department: College of Allied Health Sciences
Description: The University of Cincinnati Advanced Medical Imaging Technology major is a unique, innovative program that offers you the opportunity to become credentialed in two diagnostic medical imaging modalities, while obtaining a bachelor's degree. [2, 5] Traditionally, programs specialize in a single diagnostic medical imaging modality and most programs are housed within a certificate or associate degree programs that are 12-24 months in length. [2, 7, 8] The Advanced Medical Imaging Technology program curriculum ensures you are educated in multiple diagnostic medical imaging modalities giving you credentials in both magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and nuclear medicine technology. [2, 5] Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a technique that uses strong magnetic fields and radio waves to generate detailed images of the body. [2, 7] Nuclear medicine technology is a type of imaging that uses small amounts of radioactive substances to help creates a precise picture of the part of the body being imaged. [2, 7] Both imaging techniques help diagnosis and detect disease and analyze human anatomy. [2, 7] After completing the Baccalaureate program, you will meet national board eligibility requirements for the American registry of Radiologic Technologists (ARRT) in both MRI and nuclear medicine technology as well as the Nuclear Medicine Technology Certification Board (NMTCB) nuclear medicine exam. [2] The clinical or professional portion of the curriculum will allow you to have individualized placements at some of the best medical and imaging facilities in the region. [2, 7] You will also gain research skills that will distinguish you from other credentialed students from associate or certificate programs. [2, 7]
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati and all regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [2, 4] The Advanced Medical Imaging Technology Nuclear Medicine Technology program is currently accredited by the Joint Review Committee on Education Radiologic Technology (JRCERT) and the Joint Review Committee on Educational Programs in Nuclear Medicine Technology (JRCNMT). [2] The most recent program accreditation renewal was in 2019, the program was awarded a 7 year accreditation award and is due for review again in 2026. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Health Sciences

Description: The University of Cincinnati's online Bachelor of Science in Health Sciences degree is designed for those who have an associate degree and wish to complete their bachelor's to advance their career or prepare for a graduate program. [5] The program provides a comprehensive, interdisciplinary curriculum covering subjects like anatomy, physiology, public health, healthcare management, ethics, and research methods. [7] It aims to provide students with an in-depth science background to prepare them for further studies in fields such as physical therapy, medicine, dentistry, exercise science, occupational therapy, public health, health administration, and more. [2] The coursework is intended to build a solid foundation for graduate studies and includes rigorous courses in anatomy, physiology, and public health. [2, 7] The program is structured as an associate-to-bachelor's completion program and is ideal for those with an existing associate degree in an allied health field. [2, 5]
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati and all of its regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [7, 13] There is no specific programmatic accreditation mentioned for the Bachelor of Science in Health Sciences program itself, but other health-related programs at the university hold accreditations from bodies like the Commission on Accreditation for Health Informatics and Information Management Education (CAHIIM) and the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE). [11]
CostPerCredit: $721 per semester credit
ScholarshipType: The College of Health Solutions offers various scholarships for its students, such as the College of Health Solutions General Scholarship Fund and the Brandon Caserta Memorial Scholarship. [5, 6, 7] Scholarship applications are typically accepted between September and March for the following academic year. [6, 8]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Medical Laboratory Science
Concentration: ['Medical Laboratory Science Pre-Med Program', 'Medical Laboratory Science Co-Op Program']
Description: The University of Cincinnati Bachelor of Science in Medical Laboratory Science (BS – MLS) program will prepare you for an exciting career as a medical laboratory scientist. Medical laboratory scientists are allied health professionals who participate in patient care by performing laboratory procedures that assist in the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of diseases. The analysis performed by medical laboratory scientists uses advanced biomedical and instrumentation and technology to perform laboratory testing on blood and body fluids in the area of chemistry, microbiology, hematology, immunology, toxicology, blood banking and molecular procedures. Laboratory scientists perform manual and automated procedures and utilize laboratory information computer systems to analyze and transmit patient data. Additionally, medical laboratory scientists monitor test quality,..integrate data, problem solve, conduct research, develop new test methods and consult with other members of the health care team. The UC Medical Laboratory Science major combines a curriculum common to most undergraduate majors in the medical field with courses specific to the medical laboratory profession. The final year requires clinical rotations at partnering clinical laboratories. [2]
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati Medical Laboratory Science program is accredited by the National Accrediting Agency for Clinical Laboratory Science (NAACLS). [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nutrition & Dietetics
Bachelor of Science in Respiratory Therapy
Department: College of Allied Health Sciences

Description: The University of Cincinnati's online Bachelor of Science in Respiratory Therapy program is designed to improve real-world clinical competence while preparing active respiratory therapy professionals for a lasting future in the healthcare industry. The robust and engaging curriculum challenges students, promoting a deeper understanding of advanced healthcare operations, logistics, technology, leadership, ethics, and project management. [3] Delivered by the industry-experienced faculty in the UC College of Allied Health Sciences, the online program advances respiratory therapy practice and research by focusing on current and future industry standards. [3] The end result is a clinician who can make significant contributions to the field while positively affecting the future of respiratory care for a variety of patients. [3]
Accredidation: The Respiratory Therapy, 500015, Bachelor of Science, University of Cincinnati holds Provisional Accreditation from the Commission on Accreditation for Respiratory Care (www.coarc.com). [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Social Work
Description: The University of Cincinnati Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) program challenges students to learn about themselves and find ways to be of service in the world. The program prepares students for entry-level, generalist social work practice, giving them the knowledge and skills to work with individuals, families, groups, communities, and organizations in various settings. Social workers engage in a wide range of service areas, such as assisting families in economic distress with basic needs like food and housing, and working with individuals with physical and mental disabilities and older adults to provide care management. They also investigate allegations of child abuse and neglect, provide counseling to families, and work with children in foster care. Additionally, they help people with substance use problems recover from addiction. Upon completion, graduates are prepared for the licensing exam in Ohio to become a licensed social worker and have the foundational education for graduate study in social work. [4, 11] Through a partnership, students in the online BSW program can also gain credentials in Substance Abuse Counseling. [12]
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Social Work (online and on-campus) and Master of Social Work programs are accredited by the Council on Social Work Education's Commission on Accreditation. [2, 3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Education in Early Childhood Education
Description: The bachelor of science degree program in early childhood education prepares professionals to provide high-quality educational experiences for their community's youngest children. The Early Childhood Education Birth to Age 5 (ECE) program is designed to build on associate degree competencies to enhance professionals' ability to design and implement developmentally appropriate learning environments for children ages birth-five years. [12] Students are usually practitioners working in preschools and other child-care and educational settings. [12] Graduates will be able to facilitate positive transitions of children with disabilities and special needs, to nurture early language development and early reading and writing growth in other domains, and build early resiliency and self-regulation and to develop as early childhood stakeholder leaders. [12] Whether you are in a preschool, Head Start program, child-care center, family childcare environment, or just interested in getting started in the field, the online program provides flexibility and accessibility. [9]
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati and all regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [2, 9, 15] The educator preparation programs at the University of Cincinnati, including Early Childhood Education, are accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP). [2, 3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Criminal Justice
Description: The University of Cincinnati's Bachelor of Science in Criminal Justice program offers an interdisciplinary exploration of criminal behavior, crime prevention, and the role and function of the U.S. criminal justice system. [4] The program is designed to provide students with an understanding of criminal offending and the criminal justice process. [12] Upon completion, students are prepared for various professions in industries such as law enforcement, institutional corrections, community corrections, cybersecurity, crime analysis, loss prevention, research, law, policy, and correctional rehabilitation. [4] Students learn about the causes, correlates, and consequences of crime, and how the criminal legal system addresses it across courts, policing, and corrections. [4] The online version of the program provides a comprehensive understanding of criminal offending and the criminal justice process, combining professional skills training with relevant curriculum to develop a solid foundation of criminal justice knowledge. [3]
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati (UC) and all regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (HLC). [15] Additionally, each of its programs is approved by the Ohio Department of Higher Education (ODHE). [15]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Substance Abuse Counseling
Description: The University of Cincinnati's online Bachelor's degree in Substance Abuse Counseling prepares graduates for rewarding careers helping those who are struggling with drug and alcohol addictions. [2] It is a cutting-edge, research-oriented program that provides students with essential knowledge, competencies, and skills to kickstart careers in substance use disorder (SUD) counseling. [2] The program is designed for students who are interested in careers in the chemical dependency treatment areas of counseling and prevention. [4] Students are prepared through a program grounded in current research and proven practice in the field of substance abuse to be qualified clinicians. [4] The program meets the Ohio Chemical Dependency Professionals Board requirements for becoming a Chemical Dependency Counselor Assistant (CDCA), and also meets some of the requirements for becoming a Licensed Chemical Dependency Counselor III (LCDC III) in Ohio. [2, 4]
Accredidation: The University of Cincinnati and all regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Law and Paralegal Studies
Department: College of Education, Criminal Justice, and Human Services
Description: A bachelor's degree in law and paralegal studies opens many doors for many career opportunities, including, but not limited to, a paralegal — one of the lawyer's most valuable resources. University of Cincinnati's online Bachelor of Science in Law and Paralegal Studies program provides you with the in-demand skills needed to increase responsibility and earnings as you start or advance your legal career. [2] Paralegals perform substantive behind-the-scenes legal work that enables the law and court systems to make positive impacts on their communities. [2] Job duties vary, as there is a wide range of paralegal careers to pursue—many paralegals support lawyers by assisting with trial preparation, drafting legal documents, conducting research, and client communication. [2] Most paralegals work in law firms, but paralegal skills are also coveted by government agencies, businesses, and non-profit organizations. [2]
Accredidation: Approved by the American Bar Association (ABA). [2] The University of Cincinnati and all of its regional campuses are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [2]

Description: The Associate of Applied Business in Accounting program is a fully online, two-year associate degree program that prepares students for a career as a professional in the field of accounting. [2, 4] This program is N.E.U. Certified, meaning the courses are intentionally designed with student support and success in mind using the neuroscience of learning, evidence‑based best practices, and universal design. [2] The program emphasizes financial accounting, computerized accounting information systems, managerial accounting, payroll accounting, generally accepted accounting principles, preparation of financial statements, preparation of individual income taxes and nonprofit accounting. [3] The online program provides students with the flexibility to balance work and family obligations while advancing their education and offers a self-paced learning schedule. [2, 4]

Description: The Associate of Applied Business in Business Applications Technology program is a fully online, two-year degree program. [2, 3] After graduation you'll be prepared to enter the technology-driven workforce with in-demand skills including communication, critical thinking, data analysis, software proficiency and problem-solving. [2, 3] Business Applications Technology is the study of how businesses use data and technology in their operations. [2] If you are an early adopter who embraces the latest technology and would like to utilize it in the modern business environment, this program is for you. [2] Professionals who earn an Associate degree in Business Applications Technology perform tasks like: Facilitate scheduling; Organize and maintain files; Provide customer service; Advise vendors and co-workers; Manage projects. [2] You'll get hands-on experience with real-world applications using computer programs and business solutions like: Microsoft Word; Microsoft Excel; Microsoft Access; Microsoft PowerPoint; Microsoft Project; Tableau. Requirements: Admission to the University of Cincinnati's Associate of Individualized Study in Interdisciplinary Studies program is open to any student who wishes to design an interdisciplinary degree program using a combination of courses in multiple disciplines. New students must have a high school diploma, GED, or home-school equivalent. Transfer students can transfer up to 40 semester credit hours from a nationally or regionally accredited institution, but at least twenty credit hours must be from the University of Cincinnati. [2]
Description: The University of Cincinnati's online Associate of Individualized Study in Interdisciplinary Studies (AIS) degree program is an educational pathway with multiple fields of study, allowing students to create their own major. [2] The program allows students to tailor their studies to specific educational needs and is an excellent opportunity to use previously earned college credits towards an online associate degree. [2] The curriculum is determined by the student through participation in an academic and careers decisions seminar, where they work with a faculty advisor to integrate previously earned credits and plan new coursework covering two or more specialty concentration areas. [2] The program is 100% online and asynchronous, allowing students to log on when it is convenient. [2] It is designed for students who wish to design an individualized degree program using a combination of courses. [3] The core goal is to design an associate degree pathway that meets predetermined goals, which can be employment or continuation into a selected four-year degree program. [2]
